C.title: Fed Revamps Bank Stress Tests: What Does it Mean for U.S. Banks?
C.summary: The Federal Reserve has finalized revisions to its annual bank stress-testing framework aimed at increasing transparency and reducing volatility in capital requirements. WFC.title: Fed Revamps Bank Stress Tests: What Does it Mean for U.S. Banks?
WFC.summary: The Federal Reserve has finalized revisions to its annual bank stress-testing framework aimed at increasing transparency and reducing volatility in capital requirements. Starting in 2028, stress capital buffers (SCBs) will be calculated using two-year averages of supervisory stress tests, potentially reducing year-over-year volatility by roughly 50%. While this should provide major banks with greater visibility for capital planning, the changes are unlikely to result in broad-based capital relief, with benefits varying by institution based on trading exposure and fee-income composition.

The company has submitted a BLA to the FDA based on 36-month data, with regulatory review and durability validation as key upcoming catalysts.
